subject: card 361 retro pick: no idle between steps

architect.cite: every background wait has an armed monitor whose condition matches success, failure and expiry
architect.reply_head:
Yes

The design is minimal and bounded. It adds one Experimental entry and leaves every other value, principle and rule unchanged. The root cause is stated as "armed on success only" and "step boundary treated as a stop". Each rule in the entry answers one of those two causes.

Notes, which do not change the vote:
- Most clauses are checkable from the record: monitor conditions, the 60-second first-output read, and the trap-written end flag.
- "Idle minutes" needs a committed definition. Otherwise the retro could count it differently each time without anyone noticing.
- The counter-metric (a next step launched too early) covers the main false

qa.cite: every background wait has an armed monitor whose condition matches success, failure and expiry
qa.reply_head:
Yes

From a QA view, each rule can be shown failing before it is fixed. Card 203's crashed launcher, whose monitor only watched for "VOICES DONE", is a recorded failing case. The amendment also says outright that a check that only watches for success "is not a monitor", so a reviewer can catch that violation instead of letting it pass. The list of step boundaries (gate review after a green push, sign-off after the review, and so on) means "turn ended with the next step ready" can be checked against the records. The counter-metric guards against launching too early.

audit lens.cite: idle minutes per card and Dispatch nudges per card
audit lens.reply_head:
No
Require all monitor states, idle durations, and dispatch nudges to be committed as machine-readable artifacts per card so git history alone verifies compliance.

decider.cite: an armed, failure-aware monitor on every wait
decider.reply_head:
Yes
Evaluation rests on evidence: baseline idle and nudge counts, target 0, a counter-metric for premature launches, a defined 3-card trial, and per-retro reporting with causes. Ownership and sign-off triggers are explicit.

coach.cite: Common root: a wait is armed on success only
coach.reply_head:
Yes

Through the agile-coach lens, the proposal is the right size. It handles one concern with one Experimental entry, and it pushes the smaller findings (the Muse brief, mutation waivers, the scanner reading committed blobs, the declared-versus-ran check) into briefs and follow-up cards instead of adding them to the agreement. It draws on all seven voices plus the product owner's entry, so no perspective is missing. It has a metric, a counter-metric, a three-card trial and an owner.

architect.cite: as two committed lines in the retro document
architect.reply_head:
Yes

The amendment keeps my vote, and the regenerated patch matches the amended text. Two committed lines with a fixed format can be checked from git history alone, and they do not require committing the transient monitor states. That makes the entry easier to enforce at almost no cost. One note: a checker could falsely flag retros written before D230, so it should only check retros from the next three cards in the trial.

qa.cite: as two committed lines in the retro document
qa.reply_head:
Yes

My vote stands. I checked the regenerated patch and it has the new clause. From a QA view, the amendment makes the rule easier to test, not harder. The two committed lines, `Idle minutes: N.` and `Dispatch nudges: M.`, have a fixed pattern. A check can fail first on a retro that is missing either line or its cause line. Note: the counts are still reported by the facilitator, not measured independently, so the check proves the lines exist, not that the numbers are right.

developer.cite: a launcher's first output is read within 60 seconds
developer.reply_head:
Yes

Speaking as the backend developer: I can follow these rules every card without gaming them, and none of them weakens red, unit commits with doubles, green, flags or slice limits. The patch I read (`agreement-amendment.diff`) matches the proposal.

Notes, which don't change my vote:
- "Within 60 seconds" should be timed from the moment of launch, and the record should log that time.
- "Idle minutes" is defined as minutes with nothing running and nothing landing. A slow test run counts as running, so it doesn't push us to cut tests short.
- The counter-metric (starting a step too early and having to relaunch it) needs to stay visible in th

audit lens.cite: so that git history alone shows them.
audit lens.reply_head:
Yes
The amendment explicitly commits idle durations and dispatch nudges as documented lines, satisfying the requirement that git history alone verifies compliance. The condition is fully met.

decider.cite: every retro reports idle minutes per card
decider.reply_head:
Yes
Amendment strengthens the evidence basis: committed per-card metrics keep the trial verdict checkable from git history alone, with no change to hypothesis, counter-metric, or trial length.

coach.cite: as two committed lines in the retro document
coach.reply_head:
Yes

The amendment does not change my vote. Committing two lines per retro is lightweight and adds no extra ceremony, and it leaves monitor states out of the repository, which keeps the task force's work sized to the task. My only note is to keep each cause line to one sentence so the reporting stays proportionate.
